monthly_review.summary: This month shows a sharp shift toward higher-intensity running with significantly elevated HR and zone 4/5 time, but at the cost of volume and aerobic base maintenance compared to last month.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 4 effort jumped from 15% to 45% of total time while Zone 1+2 dropped from 53% to 10%, indicating a sudden, unsustainable shift away from foundational aerobic work.

goal_tracker.message: You need 44.5 more km across 9 additional sessions in the remaining 27 days — averaging ~5.0 km/session — to match last month’s volume.

insights.title: Efficiency declined despite faster pace
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency dropped from 13.46 to 12.54 m/sec per bpm, meaning you’re expending more HR effort per unit speed — consistent with the jump in Z4/Z5 time (22% this month vs 1% last month) and reduced Z1/Z2 recovery time.

insights.title: Over-reliance on Zone 4
insights.body: Zone 4 now accounts for 45% of total effort time (up from 15%), while Zone 1+2 collapsed to just 10% (down from 53%) — this imbalance risks fatigue accumulation and limits mitochondrial adaptation.

insights.title: Improved stride length & reduced ground contact under intensity
insights.body: Stride length increased from 68.77 cm (June 21) to 75.73–75.77 cm (July 1 & 5), and ground contact time decreased from 314 ms to 305 ms — suggesting neuromuscular adaptation to faster efforts, but vertical oscillation rose slightly (7.7 → 8.1), hinting at inefficiency under fatigue.

insights.title: High-intensity load without volume buffer
insights.body: Your July 5 run delivered 4.0 Aerobic TE at 10.0 km and 166 bpm — the highest single-session TE this period — yet occurred after only one other run in the month, indicating insufficient recovery and low chronic training load (CTL) support.

recommendations.action: Do a 6 km Zone 2 run at ≤138 bpm (based on your June avg HR of 140 and recent Z2 upper limit observed at 135–144 bpm) within next 48 hours.
recommendations.reason: To rebuild aerobic base and restore Z1/Z2 time — currently only 2% Z1 and 8% Z2 this month — and counteract the 45% Z4 dominance.

recommendations.action: Perform a 4 km easy-effort run with cadence target ≥152 spm and vertical oscillation <7.8 cm (using real-time Garmin metrics), focusing on relaxed arm swing and midfoot landing.
recommendations.reason: Your recent vertical oscillation rose to 8.0–8.1 cm during faster runs; lowering it improves efficiency and reduces injury risk, especially as cadence improved to 154 spm.

recommendations.action: Add a 15-minute post-run mobility routine (hip flexor + calf + glute activation) after your next two runs, given ground contact time dropped to 305 ms but vertical oscillation increased — a sign of compromised stability under fatigue.
recommendations.reason: Reduced ground contact without proportional efficiency gains suggests neuromuscular coordination may be stressed; targeted mobility supports sustainable form under load.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish Zone 1–2 volume to restore efficiency, lower HR drift, and prepare for future intensity with better recovery capacity.
suggested_sessions: 4 km easy-effort run with cadence & vertical oscillation focus
3 km walk-run active recovery (2 min walk / 1 min jog x 10)
